title: Beaumont revised development permit notice with consultant elevation schedule for limiting distance and permitted glazing (multi-attached residential)
jurisdiction: City of Beaumont, Alberta (development authority named on the notice; building-permit AHJ not stated)
code_edition: NBC-2019AE named in drawing note 7 (p.3). Schedule rows cite 9.10.15.4 without an edition statement. The 2023 edition is not stated in the file.
document_date: Revised notice dated January 30, 2025. Original date of decision August 13, 2021 (cover, p.1).

facts.text: The revised notice of decision (January 30, 2025) concerns a multi-attached dwelling of 85 apartments and 42 townhouses, amendment 'Change in Design Features and Wall Openings for Buildings 1-9', permit application 2021-338, status 'Approved with conditions'.
The applicant is a consultant architecture firm (EFG Architects Inc., Edmonton), and the district is Integrated Neighbourhood.
The notice states that the amendments to Development Permit 2021-338 have been conditionally approved.
Drawing note 7 reads 'ALL WINDOWS ARE CONSIDERED TO BE GUARDS AND MUST COMPLY NBC-2019AE'.

Each elevation entry cites 9.10.15.4 and lists exposed building face, limiting distance, exterior wall face area, permitted glazing percentage, total glazed or unprotected glazing (m2 and %), required fire rating and wall or cladding type.

East elevation, unit T1: limiting distance 13.87 m (between buildings); exterior wall face 9.75 m x 8.40 m = 81.90 m2; permitted glazing 100%; total glazed openings 1.12 m2 (= 1.38%); 'REQ. FIRE RATING: NONE (45 MIN PROVIDED)'.
North elevation, unit T1: limiting distance 4.72 m / 2 = 2.36 m (between buildings); exterior wall face 6.13 m x 8.71 m = 53.39 m2; permitted glazing 9%; total unprotected glazing 4.84 m2 (= 9%).
Other entries halve the limiting distance to a property line or between buildings, for example west elevation, unit T3: 2.4 m / 2 = 1.2 m (property line) with permitted glazing 7%.
Condition 21 states the proposed development must meet or exceed the requirements of the current Alberta Building Codes, Alberta Fire Codes and NFPA1141.
The same elevation schedule format recurs on pp.31-34 with different unit values. Which sheets are approved and which are proposed was not reconciled in this lane.
